fields.rationale: TileLink is a purely digital, synchronous on-chip interconnect protocol. It does not specify any analog signaling, DC electrical specifications, AC timing parameters (Vih/Vil/tsu/th/etc.), or IO standards (LVCMOS / LVDS / etc.). All channels are defined in terms of logical levels sampled on the rising edge of the shared clock signal.

signaling_summary.clock: Single 'clock' input signal per TileLink link; both master and slave interfaces sample on the rising edge.
signaling_summary.reset: Single 'reset' input signal, active HIGH; may be asserted asynchronously, must be deasserted synchronous with rising clock edge.
signaling_summary.signal_naming_convention: All TileLink signals other than clock and reset consist of the channel identifier (a-e) followed by an underscore followed by the signal name (e.g. a_opcode, d_data, e_sink). For devices with multiple TileLink interfaces, signal names should be prefixed with a descriptive token plus underscore (e.g. gpio_a_opcode).
signaling_summary.io_count_per_channel: Each channel is unidirectional. Bus is non-tristate.
signaling_summary.default_state_during_reset: All valid signals must be driven LOW during reset for at least 100 cycles; ready/control/data signals are free to take any value during reset.

fields.notes: Per-implementation electrical specs (clock period, IO standards, signal integrity, max-skew, max-fanout) are defined by the SoC integrator outside the TileLink spec.

evidence.quote: TileLink is a synchronous bus protocol. Both master interface and slave interface on a TileLink link must share the same clock, reset, and power.
